_README: The SECOND Cost_Pilot of task 11.18, re-run because the first pilot's design set was not
representative of the wall clock a legitimate run may spend. Run:
The first pilot (.eval-runs/property-only-cost-pilot/, left in place as evidence) measured
three EASY designs and recorded a Per_Design_Extrapolation of 1250 tokens and 8227 ms, which
sets the Anomaly_Guard at 82270 ms. The shipped Property_Time_Budget is 150000 ms, and a
design that spends nearly all of it is already measured: multi_booth_8bit reached
proof-timeout at 149997 ms under that same ceiling. A guard about 11x TIGHTER than the
budget a run may legitimately spend would halt the full population on its first hard design
and call a measured proof-timeout a suspected defect.
No credential belongs in this file. It is read from the Credential_File alone, with no
environment fallback, and no config field can hold it.
extrapolationFrom is null, which is what confines this run to the Cost_Pilot: while no
Per_Design_Extrapolation is recorded, nothing outside the three designs below dispatches.
The Per_Design_Extrapolation this run records is the MAXIMUM of its per-design figures, and
a loose guard is the intended outcome rather than a figure to tune: the maximum puts the
guard where no plausible variation between designs can trip it, which is what makes an
actual trip information about the run.
_costPilotDesignIds: Three designs, each confirmed present in the pinned checkout and absent from the Stage 0
quarantine, so each is one of the 46 scored. multi_booth_8bit is the HARD one and the whole
point of this re-run; adder_8bit and counter_12 are carried over from the first pilot so the
two runs stay comparable, and counter_12 keeps a sequential design in the set.
